title: 34 bricks, counted in seconds
_map: Bundles of ten (Y2) + The counter that rolls over (Y1). Big idea: 34 = 3 tens and 4 ones, and other ways too; after 9 ones comes a new ten.
_story: Steve dropped a bucket of 34 bricks and wants to count them fast. Snapping rods of ten is the trick (like Minecraft stacks of 64, but tens). He makes 34 different ways, then the farm counter rolls past 39 and 99.
_stepChain: counting one by one is slow → snap 10 into a rod → 34 = rods + singles → the digits mean tens and ones → 34 made other ways (break a rod) → Steve thinks 2 tens and 14 ones is a different number → 39 + 1 rolls over → 99 + 1

talk.goodAnswer: 3 tens: three rods of 10 bricks. The 4 means 4 single bricks.

talk.ask: Can you make 34 in a different way?
talk.goodAnswer: yes, like 2 tens and 14 ones, or 1 ten and 24 ones. It's still 34 bricks.
the 10 ones snap together into a new ten, so it's 4 tens and 0 ones.

handsOn: Build rods of 10 Lego bricks. Make 34 with rods and single bricks. Then break one rod and make 34 a different way. Can you make 34 with no rods at all?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Oh no! Crash! I dropped my bucket of bricks! There are 34 of them, all over the floor. Counting them one by one takes forever! Is there a faster way?

Here's a builder's trick! Snap 10 bricks together into a long rod. Click, click, click! Then another rod. And another! 3 rods of 10, and 4 bricks left over. A rod of 10 is called a ten. A single brick is called a one.
Now look at the number 34. Each digit has its own job! The 3 says: 3 tens, 3 rods. The 4 says: 4 ones, 4 single bricks. 3 rods, 4 bricks. 34!
Can you make 34 a different way? Pick how many rods to keep, then tap the hammer. The other bricks stay as ones. Find all the ways!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Wait a minute! 2 tens and 14 ones. That looks totally different from 34! That must be a different number. Right?

question.prompt: Is 2 tens and 14 ones the same as 34?
question.onRight: Yes! Breaking a rod doesn't make any bricks disappear. 20 and 14 is still 34!

1.mistake: thinks changing how it's grouped changes the amount
1.hint: When the rod broke, did any bricks go away? Count the ones: 10 and 4.
1.say: We only broke one rod into single bricks. No bricks ran away! 2 tens is 20, and 14 more makes 34.

question.reveal: 2 tens and 14 ones is 34! Same bricks, grouped a different way.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: My farm counter counts my chickens. It says 39. That's 3 tens and 9 ones. Ooh, look! One more chicken is coming! Bawk!

question.prompt: What will the counter say now? Make a guess!
question.reveal: 40! 9 ones and 1 more make 10 ones. And 10 ones snap together into a new ten! Click! So it's 4 tens and 0 ones: 40. The ones go back to zero, and the tens go up!

narration.text: Here's a challenge for later. Invent your very own counter! It could count in tens, like ours. Or in fives! What happens when your counter fills up?

rule.ask: What does the 3 in 34 mean? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: In 34, the 3 means 3 tens, and the 4 means 4 ones. And 10 ones always snap together into a new ten.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! The counter says 99. One more chicken arrives. What does it say now?
bonus.reveal: 100! 10 ones make a new ten. Then 10 tens snap together into something brand new: a hundred!
